 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. For the first time in twenty-four years, the Colorado Avalanche are hosting a game on Halloween!
 Tonight will be a rematch against the Calgary Flames, who have been heating up of late with five wins in their previous six games.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Colorado Avalanche (7-5-1)
 The Opponent : Calgary Flames (6-7-0)
 Time : 8:00 P.M. MDT/10:00 P.M. EDT
 Watch : ALT, ALT+ (Avalanche Local Broadcast Area), ESPN+, NHL Center Ice (Outside Regional Broadcast Area – US), SN, SN+ (Canadian National Broadcast)
 Listen : Altitude Sports Radio KKSE-FM 92.5 FM
 Colorado Avalanche
 The Avalanche, looking more Dr. Jekyll than Mr. Hyde, defeated the visiting New Jersey Devils by a 5-2 decision on Wednesday night, avenging their loss at the Prudential Center eight nights earlier. New Jersey, playing the second half of a back-to-back series, started goaltender Jake Allen, who gave up five goals on forty-five shots. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped twenty of twenty-two shots for his sixth win of the season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Nicolas Roy, who had missed the previous six games with injury, returned to the lineup, registering an assist on Nazem Kadri's go-ahead goal in the second period. Defenseman Josh Manson, however, did not finish the game. Head coach Jared Bednar announced yesterday that Manson would miss eight weeks with an ankle injury.
 Manson's absence paves the way for increased usage for defenseman Noah Juulsen. Juulsen has played eight games for Colorado this season.
 It's likely that Blackwood closes out the home stand, saving Scott Wedgewood for next week. They kick off another back-to-back pair of road games on Monday in Chicago before heading to Columbus.
 MacKinnon still leads all skaters in points (22) and assists (14). Artturi Lehkonen leads the team in goals (10).
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement A win tonight pulls the Avs within one point of second-place Utah in the Central Division standings. The Avs won the opening game of the season series against Calgary on October 08.

 Forwards:
Artturi Lehkonen – Nathan MacKinnon – Martin Nečas

 Defense:

Brett Kulak – Sam Malinski
Noah Juulsen – Brent Burns
 Between the Pipes:
Mackenzie Blackwood
Scott Wedgewood
 Calgary Flames
 Calgary's start to the season was anything but hot: they lost six of their first seven games of the season, including the previously-mentioned 7-3 loss on home ice to Colorado on October 08. During their most recent four game homestand, however, things started to heat up. Thanks to stellar play by goaltender Devin Cooley, Calgary swept all four games, which featured victories over Minnesota, Toronto, and the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Unfortunately, Cooley's heater came to an abrupt end this past Wednesday after sustaining an injury from a collision with Edmonton's Colton Dach. Calgary wound up losing by a 4-0 decision, but rebounded last night on home ice with a 6-2 victory over the Seattle Kraken. Goaltender Dustin Wolf recorded his first win in over two weeks, saving twenty-five of twenty-seven shots against.
 Calgary, who has been without left wing Jonathan Huberdeau after he underwent hip resurfacing surgery last season, is seeing injuries continue to pile up. Left wing Samuel Honzek, who last played against Colorado, is listed as week-to-week. Brennan Othmann also was injured during the Edmonton game after a fight with Ty Emberson.
 With Cooley also listed as week-to-week, goaltender Arsenii Sergeev has been called up from the AHL's Calgary Wranglers to back up Wolf. Maxim Tsyplakov, who had been a healthy scratch for Calgary's previous five games, returned to the lineup against Seattle.
 Joel Farabee and Matt Coronato lead all Calgary skaters in points (14). Rookie Matvei Gridin leads the team in goals (5), while Coronato leads the team in assists (11). Right wing Adam Klapka leads all Calgary skaters in penalty minutes (37), second only to Ottawa's Nick Cousins (42) across the League.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Tonight's game marks the start of a three game road trip for Calgary, and is their only visit to Denver. They return home to start a three game homestand on Thursday.
